notes:
Summary: Enterprise ecommerce platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency recommendation and chat features. Primary driver: predictable tail latency and reserved throughput for peak sale events (Black Friday-like traffic spikes).

Key requirements / asks (from CTO & infra lead):
- Throughput guarantees during flash sales: target 10k req/s across recommendation routes, sustained 2M tokens/min during peaks.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 20ms for embeddings lookups, p95 < 70ms for reranking, p99 < 150ms for recommendation generation. Hard cutover if >200ms p99.
- Reserved GPU planning: want recommendation cluster sized for 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (plus 2x burst GPUs), separate pool for customer-facing chat.
- Multi-tenant isolation: strict tenant isolation between business units (B2B vs marketplace sellers) with enforcement at network and runtime level.
- Traffic shaping / priority lanes: need Gold/Silver/Bronze lanes per route; checkout-critical routes (checkout recs / fraud scoring) get preemptive priority.
- Per-route quotas: per-API-key QPS + token budgets, ability to apply token-bucket shaping and rate-limited retry windows.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: auto-throttling if a tenant exceeds 70% of dedicated pool or if tail latency impact detected; support for soft-preemption and token-pricing incentives.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), audit logs on per-request basis, KMS for key separation, data residency in us-east.
- Fallback & routing: automatic fallback to smaller quantized model for low-priority lanes in overload scenarios; cross-region fallback acceptable but must preserve data residency for certain routes.

- 2026-02-18: Intro call (AE Maya) — overview of dedicated + pricing model.
- 2026-02-24: Architecture deep-dive with infra team (SE Diego present) — discussed reserved GPU math and instance types. Fireflies: ff-20260224-79b3. Notes: "If we can't hit p99 150ms, team will own building in-house cache layer."

Traffic shaping & priority lanes (draft design points from Redwood SE):
- Priority lanes: define three priority classes (gold/silver/bronze) enforced at edge router + runtime token-bucket. Gold has dedicated concurrency shares and preemption rights; silver has reserved baseline and elastic burst; bronze best-effort.
- Per-route quotas: attach route-level QPS and token budgets to API key metadata; enforcement via admission controller. Ability to assign multiple routes to same priority pool.
- Tenant isolation: runtime uses cgroup-like scheduling on GPUs + KV cache partitioning to avoid cache pollution. Network isolation via VPC endpoints and per-tenant subnet assignments.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: detection by tracing/p99 delta across tenants; automated mitigation: (1) throttle offending tenant to its baseline, (2) migrate heavy workloads to burst GPUs, (3) when persistent, trigger rate-limited backpressure and alert ops.
- Shaping primitives: leaky-bucket for sustained rate limits, token-bucket for bursty traffic, and per-route circuit-breakers for overload.
- SLA Guarantees: proposed SLAs tied to reserved GPU count (example: 4 reserved GPUs -> 99.9% uptime and p95 latency caps; penalties defined per 30-day window).

Negotiation points / open questions for Redwood legal & SRE:
- Exact definition of p99 measurement window and allowed exclusions (warm-up, scheduled rolling upgrades).
- Remedies for noisy-neighbor incidents beyond credits — request for guaranteed mitigation timeline (e.g., mitigation action within 15 minutes of detection).
- Burst capacity pricing and billing model for burst GPUs during flash sales.
- Data residency exceptions for cross-region fallback on non-customer-identifiable data.

Technical blockers and risks:
- Need more detail on how runtime enforces per-tenant KV cache partitioning — infra team skeptical of cache contamination claims.
- Procurement wants numeric guarantees for degraded-mode fallback (how much latency increase allowed when downgrading to quantized model).
- Security requires architecture diagram with KMS key separation and audit log retention policy (30/90/365 days options).
